title: Owe Taxes? How to Pay Without a Credit Card

lines.say: You did your taxes, and you owe.
Before you reach for a credit card, let's compare the options, with real numbers.

scene.label: Tax bill due in April
scene.sub: with $450 a month to pay it down

lines.cap: Our example: a $2,400 tax bill, and $450 a month to put toward it.
lines.say: Our example: a twenty-four hundred dollar tax bill, and four fifty a month to put toward it.
Rule number one comes before any of the math.
File on time, even if you can't pay.

lines.cap: The penalty for filing late is usually much bigger than for paying late: generally 5% of the unpaid tax per month, versus 0.5%. On $2,400, that's about $120 a month, versus $12.
lines.say: The penalty for filing late is usually much bigger than the penalty for paying late. Generally five percent of the unpaid tax per month, versus half a percent. On twenty-four hundred, that's about a hundred twenty a month, versus twelve.

scene.text: Can't pay? File on time anyway.

lines.say: So file by the deadline no matter what. Then pick how to pay.
Option one. Put it on a credit card.

lines.cap: Card payment processors charge a fee, often around 2%: about $45 here. Then 24% interest. Paying $450 a month, it's about $215 in total.
lines.say: Card payment processors charge a fee, often around two percent. About forty-five dollars here. Then twenty-four percent interest. Paying four fifty a month, it's about two hundred fifteen dollars in total.
Option two. An IRS payment plan.

lines.cap: If you can pay within 180 days, the IRS short-term plan has no setup fee. You still owe interest (7% a year as of late 2026) plus the small late-payment penalty.
lines.say: If you can pay within a hundred and eighty days, the IRS short-term plan has no setup fee. You still owe interest, seven percent a year as of late twenty twenty-six, plus the small late-payment penalty.

lines.cap: Same six months. About $86 instead of $215.
lines.say: Same six months. About eighty-six dollars instead of two fifteen.

scene.text: Apply at IRS.gov. Check the current fees first.

lines.cap: Longer plans exist too, with a setup fee that's lower if you apply online with automatic payments. Rates and fees change, so check IRS.gov before you apply.
lines.say: Longer plans exist too, with a setup fee that's lower if you apply online with automatic payments. Rates and fees change, so check IRS dot gov before you apply.
And option three. Don't owe next year.

lines.cap: Owing usually means too little was withheld. Adjust your W-4 so a little more comes out of each check: $2,400 over 26 paychecks is about $92 each.
lines.say: Owing usually means too little was withheld. Adjust your W-4 so a little more comes out of each check. Twenty-four hundred over twenty-six paychecks is about ninety-two dollars each.
Freelance or side income? Set the tax aside every time you're paid. Episode thirty-one covers it.
